notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Inspect existing module conventions before implementing: Reading sibling functions in the target file reveals required helpers and patterns like to_money, ZERO, and round_money.
  Before writing a new function, read the surrounding module (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to see how money is normalized and rounded. Mirror those conventions so the new function is consistent and passes hidden tests.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty collections with the project's zero constant: For aggregate functions over possibly-empty lists, return the module's ZERO constant rather than a literal 0 or Decimal(0).
  Guard against division by zero by checking total quantity first and returning ZERO. Use sum(..., ZERO) as the start value so the accumulator stays a Decimal and matches project style.
- [rb-0001] Use project money helpers for rounding: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
  Python's round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals. Always import and call ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent) on any computed money value before returning it.

item.title: Mirror existing error codes and validation order from sibling functions
item.description: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and state-check-first pattern rather than inventing new ones.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same message format and check ordering used by analogous functions like issue_invoice/authorize. This keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on error codes.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer inputs in Python
item.description: isinstance(True, int) is True, so explicitly reject bools before the int check.
item.content: When a parameter must be a positive integer, write `if isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0: raise ...` — otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0 and hidden tests for invalid quantity will fail.

item.title: Normalize money via round_money before range checks
item.description: Convert unit_price with the project's round_money helper, then compare against ZERO, so string/float inputs and rounding are handled uniformly.
item.content: Accept flexible price inputs by calling round_money(unit_price) first, then validate `price < ZERO` and store the rounded Decimal on the LineItem. This matches how line_total and authorize handle amounts and avoids type errors on raw strings/floats.
